---
title: Missing Values Placeholders
---

#### 🧭 Introduction

A Missingness Heat-map is a visual tool for exploring tabular data. It highlights missing values and also flags __candidate__ missing-value placeholders (e.g. -99, --, N/A).
These candidates are configured in the sidebar and are typically data-type specific.
	
 > Placeholders = values used to stand in for “no data” when a value is required e.g. integers: -99, -999; floats: -99.0; strings: --, N/A; date-times: 0001-01-01.

The any buttons in the footer allow any named placeholders to be converted to missing values throughout the dataset.

#### 🏞️ Front

The card's front shows a heat-map chart of potential placeholders, as well as missingness. Buttons allow the substitution of each potential 
placeholder.

#### 🔄 Flip side

The back of the card tabulates the count of each placeholder per variable.

#### ⚙️ Settings

Use the Tour Guide button to learn about the settings of this card.

#### 🎯 Goals

 1. _Primary:_ Help you verify whether candidate placeholders truly represent missingness (a domain-aware judgment).
 1. _Secondary:_ Make it easy to fix the data. For each detected placeholder, the card provides a button to replace those values with an unambiguous missing value. The chart and table refresh to verify the efficacy of the operation. 

***
All cards downstream of this card will receive any changes enacted by this card. At most, these changes will produce additional missing values.
